targets.title: Functional annotation of a novel NFKB1 promoter polymorphism that increases risk for ulcerative colitis.
targets.evidence_quote: We first set out to confirm the published associations of , susceptibility to CD or UC with NFKB1 and TLR4 alleles. Specifically, we attempted to replicate the putative association of the -94delATTG allele of NFKB1 (NFKB1 94delATTG) with UC and the 299Gly allele of TLR4 (TLR4299G1y) with CD and UC.24,25
targets.outcome_quote: In terms of the putative NFKB1 94delATTG risk allele, Karban et al.25 first reported an association with risk of developing UC. We therefore tested this specific hypothesis in our entire set of samples but did not find significant evidence of association (OR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.81-1.2; Supplementary Table 2).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The paper’s own samples did not support the original UC association; the pooled literature finding is not the outcome of the new-sample replication.
